identity.life_stage: married, no children yet, dental hygienist

engagement.interaction_backstory: She sings on the vocal team every third Sunday and found the catalog hunting for something her 400-seat room could actually pull off without a click track. She listens the way a student studies — same song eleven times, learning the runs. What she needs and cannot find is a key, a BPM, and a stems-or-instrumental version, and she has typed that question into the search bar four separate times.

depth.core_contradiction: Runs the vocal rotation better than anyone and has never once volunteered to sing lead, and tells herself it is humility.
depth.wound: At twenty-four a worship pastor told her, in front of the team, that she was 'a great blend voice.' She has never gotten past the word blend.
depth.longing: To be asked. Not to audition — asked.
depth.faith_journey: Southern Baptist from the cradle, VBS to youth camp to team; no crisis, no drift, and a growing suspicion that untested faith is not the same as strong faith.
depth.voice_fingerprint: Bullet-points a text message; says 'just so I'm tracking'; ends questions with 'or no?'
depth.open_doubt: Whether the excellence culture at her church is worship or production, and whether she would know the difference from inside it.

social_graph.name: Kyle

depth.emotional_weather_default: Bright and efficient; quiet and clipped for a day after she sings.
depth.daily_texture: 6am gym, patients until four, Thursday rehearsal, the practice playlist in the car with the windows up.
depth.sensory_anchor: A church van at 2am coming back from camp, everyone asleep but the two people singing quietly in the back.
depth.living_arc: One honest conversation away from asking for a lead, or from quitting the team entirely.
